interest: This cross-reference sheet illustrates how U.S. diplomatic posts monitored agricultural production and economic competition between China and Japan during the Second Sino-Japanese War. It is particularly interesting for documenting the involvement of British technical expert P. E. Witham as an adviser to Chinese wartime trade entities (the Chinese Foreign Trade Commission and the China National Tea Corporation), shedding light on international technical assistance and wartime tea export strategies.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department document file sheet (cross-reference note) dated January 6, 1939, filed under decimal file 894.61332 (Japan, Tea). It directs researchers to document 893.61332/15 for Despatch No. 362 from the American Consulate General in Hong Kong (under Addison E. Southard). The referenced despatch forwards a comparative memorandum prepared by P. E. Witham, British technical adviser to the Chinese Foreign Trade Commission and the China National Tea Corporation, analyzing and comparing the Chinese and Japanese tea industries during the years 1937 and 1938 amidst the Second Sino-Japanese War.

subfiles.summary: This cross-reference note records Despatch No. 362 dated January 6, 1939, from Addison E. Southard in Hong Kong, filed under China decimal file 893.61332/15. The despatch encloses a memorandum compiled by P. E. Witham, a British technical adviser to the Chinese Foreign Trade Commission and the China National Tea Corporation. The memorandum presents a comparative study of the tea industries in China and Japan across 1937 and 1938.
